note:
Reviewed CDB90 match 94, pinned revision e0b35ec4d798cec3bb4e6970c0f6bb7aa69e2f4c. CDB90 (CAA Database of Battles, Version 1990), tidy data maintained by Jeffrey B. Arnold. Original US Army Concepts Analysis Agency data; revised data licensed ODC-BY. Original force designations and strength interpretations are retained with each quantity. Each side is one aggregate force, including any coalition; its total is not allocated among members. Personnel casualties are not deaths. Source estimates and adjudged error margins are not statistical confidence intervals. Equipment and tactical movements are not established by this dataset. Match review: Exact linked article, named engagement and complete source first/last day match the catalogue. The row is parentless, with no competing source row for this target. Preserve the two original source NAM force identities; counts remain CDB estimates.

The locally named British force in the American Revolutionary War receives the existing cocked-hat flintlock infantry family. A surviving British Pattern 1769 musket and National Park Service weapons interpretation support the period armament; no exact battalion equipment issue is asserted. The model is a representative infantry component, not an exact regimental uniform or a statement that every soldier used that equipment. Coalition identities, component proportions, CDB 90 personnel evidence and all loss categories remain unchanged.

The locally named American force at Hobkirk’s Hill 1781 receives the existing Continental musket-bearing family, using the National Park Service’s contemporary Southern Campaign equipment interpretation as an explicit analogy. Militia clothing, rifles and other arms are not assigned proportions. The model is a representative infantry component, not an exact regimental uniform or a statement that every soldier used that equipment. Coalition identities, component proportions, CDB 90 personnel evidence and all loss categories remain unchanged.
